subject: Post-demo: feature chargeback & unit-econ assumptions
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lewis <samantha.lewis@meditrack.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: feature chargeback & unit-econ assumptions

Hi Samantha — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and the items we promised to document so your finance and product teams can validate economics. Short version up front: we'll need ballpark monthly token volumes by feature, an initial target $/1M-tokens you want to budget to (you mentioned a range), and any constraints for CAC payback / margin targets so we can shape a pricing proposal.

Notes from the call:
- Primary feature: "Clinical Summary Generator" (embedded in patient portal) — expected usage: push notifications + on-demand summaries.
- Secondary: "Provider Q&A" (internal-facing) — lower volume, higher per-interaction token count.
- Token shape: median session ~1.2k tokens; top 5% sessions ~6k tokens.
- You said the initial target budget is roughly $2k–$6k/month for inference per feature in PoC, and long-term target is around $10–$12/1M tokens at product scale (is that still correct?).

What we need from you (action items):
1) Confirm expected monthly active users for Clinical Summary generator in PoC and target production (MAU_PoC / MAU_Prod).
2) Confirm target $/1M tokens you want us to use for pricing scenarios (you mentioned $10–$12). If you have a hard cap for PoC, call it out.
3) Any internal CAC/payback constraints? You mentioned a 6–9 month payback target for the new feature — confirm.
4) If procurement requires an SOW or a budget code, send that to Aaron and cc us.

I've attached a quick econ worksheet and a draft unit-econ one-pager that maps $/1M tokens to $/feature (we use a simple formula: feature_cost = tokens_per_session * sessions_per_month * $/token). I populated three scenarios (PoC conservative, PoC optimistic, Prod baseline) using the rough numbers from today.

Next steps from our side: once you send MAU estimates and confirm the $/1M target, Karthik will produce a short pricing scenario (3 lanes: hosted pay-as-you-go, reserved capacity for predictable throughput, and a dedicated private option). We'll also show estimated CAC payback given your conversion assumptions.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min follow-up if that's easier than back-and-forth.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: meditrack-metrics-sheet.xlsx, redwood-feature-econ-v1.pdf

Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: feature chargeback & unit-econ assumptions

Thanks Neha — appreciate the write-up. Quick clarifications:
- MAU_PoC (clinical summary): 1,200 users (pilot internal clinics). MAU_Prod target: 42,000 (full rollout across network).
- Average sessions/month per MAU: 1.6 (patients access summary 1–2x).
- Median tokens/session ~1.1k, we measured with current prototype; peak sessions can reach ~5.5k tokens.
- Budget for PoC inference: cap $5k/month across features.
- Long-term finance target: yes, aiming for ~$10/1M tokens (engineering prefers that number for forecasting).
- CAC/payback: leadership wants new feature payback within 9 months; ideal is 6 months but not mandatory for PoC.

Aaron will share procurement contact info and internal budget code later today.

Samantha
Samantha Lewis
Director, Product Operations, MediTrack
samantha.lewis@meditrack.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aaron Cho <aaron.cho@meditrack.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: feature chargeback & unit-econ assumptions

Thanks Samantha — that's super helpful. I've re-run the three scenario rows in the attached worksheet using the numbers you gave and pulled out the headline $/feature. Summary below (all $ rounded):

Scenario A — PoC conservative (cap $5k/mo)
- MAU: 1,200; sessions/user/month 1.6 => sessions/mo = 1,920
- tokens/session median: 1.1k => tokens/mo = ~2.11M tokens
- If finance target is $10/1M tokens -> monthly inference cost = $21.1 (this is wrong — need to double-check, hold on)

[----- Neha's quick correction inline below -----]
Correction: I had a formula slip above; correct math: tokens/mo = sessions * tokens/session = 1,920 * 1,100 = 2,112,000 tokens. At $10 per 1,000,000 tokens -> cost = (2,112,000 / 1,000,000) * $10 = $21.12 total per month.

Scenario A result: monthly inference cost ~= $21.12 (well under your $5k PoC cap). That suggests inference is not the dominant cost for PoC; integration and engineering/time-to-value will be the levers.

Scenario B — PoC optimistic (higher session length)
- if median tokens/session = 2.5k and sessions/mo = 1,920 => tokens/mo = 4.8M => inference cost at $10/1M = ~$48.

Scenario C — Prod baseline (MAU 42k, sessions/user/month 1.6)
- sessions/mo = 67,200; tokens/mo = 67,200 * 1,100 = 73.92M tokens
- inference cost at $10/1M = $739.20/month for the feature

Takeaway: even at production scale, at $10/1M tokens inference spend for this single feature is modest relative to typical feature budgets. Larger drivers: SLA requirements (low-latency hosted vs. reserved GPU), and whether you need encryption/HSM/private deployment which will change price.

CAC payback illustration (very rough):
- If the feature drives 2% incremental conversion on a cohort with 5k new users/month and average LTV of $120 => incremental revenue/month = 0.02 * 5,000 * $120 = $12,000. If Redwood add-on + infra costs = $1,000/month initially (worst-case), payback occurs within month 1 — so payback is sensitive to conversion assumptions. We'll build a sensitivity table.

Next actions I propose:
- Karthik will produce a 1-page pricing scenarios doc that maps your $10/1M target to hosted vs reserved vs private, and show estimated monthly costs for PoC and Prod.
- Marissa will draft a short note on likely margin impact and suggested billing SKU (feature chargeback per MAU vs per-session).
- Samantha/Aaron: share the procurement contact and any budget code.

Would you prefer a short call Wednesday to walk the pricing lanes or should we send a one-pager first?

Best,
Neha

Subject: Re: Post-demo: feature chargeback & unit-econ assumptions

Hi Samantha — looping in a short pricing note (attached as redwood-feature-econ-v1.pdf). Key bullets:
- If your target is $10/1M tokens we can easily meet that in hosted pay-as-you-go for PoC; your $5k cap is far above inference spend for the pilot (see Neha's calcs).
- Reserved capacity starts to make sense when you need predictable tail latency and sustained throughput (beyond ~50M tokens/mo). For your projected Prod ~74M tokens/mo, reserved or dedicated brings cost stability and lower per-token unit economics in exchange for commitment.
- Private (VPC/on-prem) option increases unit costs (engineering + infra) but may be required for compliance; we can model it as a premium of 2x–3x token cost depending on deployment.

Quick ask: Marissa, can you confirm what billing SKU you'd like us to propose (per-MAU feature charge vs per-session token pass-through)? My recommendation: per-feature MAU for customer-facing product because it's simpler for commercial teams to reason about, and then we provide a token-based internal breakdown for chargeback.

Samantha — happy to run a 20-min pricing review Wednesday 10:00–10:30 PT. If that works I'll send a calendar invite and a 1-page spreadsheet with 3 lanes.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-feature-econ-v1.pdf
